front-end function for taking a list of windowed time series by mask value, interpolating them onto a time grid, and (optionally) averaging across voxels/units within a value to derive the mean interpolated time series

Source: R/event_lock_timeseries.R
get_medusa_interpolated_ts.Rd

front-end function for taking a list of windowed time series by mask value, interpolating them onto a time grid, and (optionally) averaging across voxels/units within a value to derive the mean interpolated time series

Usage

get_medusa_interpolated_ts(
  fmri_obj,
  event = NULL,
  time_before = -3,
  time_after = 3,
  collide_before = NULL,
  collide_after = NULL,
  pad_before = -1.5,
  pad_after = 1.5,
  output_resolution = NULL,
  group_by = "trial",
  time_audit = FALSE,
  overlap_policy = NULL,
  valid_col = NULL,
  neighbor_events = NULL,
  max_gap = NULL,
  readout_kernel = "linear",
  readout_width = NULL
)

Arguments

fmri_obj

an fmri_ts object containing a single run of data with corresponding events

event

the event to which the fmri time series should be aligned (column in fmri_obj$event_data)

time_before

How many seconds before the event do we want data. Default: -3

time_after

How many seconds after the event do we want data. Default: 3

collide_before

An optional vector of column names in trial_df that set a boundary on the earliest time point used in interpolation. This effectively truncates the time series for interpolation to a smaller window than specified by time_before.

collide_after

An optional vector of column names in trial_df that set a boundary on the latest time point used in interpolation. This effectively truncates the time series for interpolation to a smaller window than specified by time_after.

pad_before

Number of seconds to include in the epoch time window before the event of interest. Interpolation spans the window from time_before to time_after, but padding includes data points at the boundary that can help provide sufficient data to interpolate early and late times within the epoch.

pad_after

Number of seconds to include in the epoch time window after the event of interest.

output_resolution

Time step, in seconds, for the interpolated data. Defaults to the repetition time stored in fmri_obj.

group_by

return interpolated time series for each combination of group_by variables. Default is to provide one interpolated time series per trial.

time_audit

If TRUE, additional columns will be added to the output showing how alignment is calculated vis-a-vis event timing

overlap_policy

One of "allow", "truncate", or "exclude". NULL uses truncation when collision columns are supplied and allows overlap otherwise. Explicit allow retains full windows. Exclude removes whole epochs whose closed requested windows overlap another target epoch, including ties.

valid_col

Optional logical source-data column. FALSE or NA censors that row for all value columns without deleting its acquisition time.

neighbor_events

Event columns used for nearest-event annotations; defaults to the target event column. Does not itself censor observations.

max_gap

Maximum interpolation bracket duration in seconds, defaulting to the acquisition TR. Explicit invalid rows always block interpolation; this tolerance only permits wider brackets across deleted rows.

readout_kernel

Readout kernel applied at each output grid time: "linear" (default two-point bracket interpolation), "boxcar", "triangle", or "gaussian" local window integration within each contiguous uncensored segment.

readout_width

Full window width (in seconds) for non-linear readout_kernel modes. Defaults to 1.5 * max_gap.

Details

The interpolation grid includes zero and remains within the requested interval, including zero-width and one-sided windows. When trial is a grouping variable, missing and unsupported epochs retain missing estimates and an epoch_status column: "ok", "partial", "insufficient_data", "missing_onset", "outside_run", "censored", or "no_data". These describe timing and available output support, not physiological isolation from other trials. Interpolation occurs within each unit before aggregation, preserving explicit missing rows and acquisition gaps. Off-grid median/SD now summarize the interpolated units. Each value has contributor/reason counts, source IDs, and the maximum distinct-epoch reuse count. Source IDs index observed acquisition times within this run; reuse is computed within the returned grouping. The source_clock attribute maps IDs to absolute acquisition times. Epoch annotations beginning with align_ are always included when trial is a grouping variable. They describe timing, not physiological attribution. Whole-window exclusion adds "overlap_excluded" to epoch statuses.
